A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SinGeo and contain readable main text, equations, 13 tables, eight figures, and supplementary Sections A–H. All 14 pages of each version support comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original SinGeo benchmark evaluations, ablations, consistency measurements, and qualitative analyses in the main text and supplementary material.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experimental results, including evaluations on four datasets and the supplementary ablations.

M1.justification: The dual discriminative architecture, transformations, losses, and curriculum formulation remain unchanged. The revised rotation-probability endpoints in Section 5.1 correct reported experimental settings without establishing a redesigned method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate CVUSA, CVACT, VIGOR, and University-1652 with the same orientation, FoV, geographic-split, and retrieval-task coverage, including supplementary evaluations.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in corresponding experiments. This includes the main benchmark comparisons and both ConGeo[360] and ConGeo[180] variants in supplementary Table 11.

E3.justification: Section 5.1 changes the reported satellite-rotation probability endpoints from p_init=100%, p_final=25% to p_init=0%, p_final=75%. This is a substantive correction to one training setting; the PDFs do not establish that experiments were rerun. Other protocols remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The DDL/CL ablations in Table 7, rotation/scheduling/loss-weight studies in Tables 8–10, alternative consistency measurements in Table 13, and qualitative cases are retained unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The same point-estimate reporting practice is retained.

E6.justification: Reported results in Tables 1–13 and the qualitative comparisons are unchanged. For example, SinGeo's average R@1 remains 79.1 on CVUSA in Table 1 and 35.8 on CVACT Test in Table 11. The revised rotation probabilities are settings, not result values.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(7), including the losses, curriculum schedules, and consistency definitions, remain unchanged. No mathematical assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added or removed.

C1.justification: The first contribution bullet is rewritten to emphasize the existing DDL–curriculum combination. The abstract still retains the first-use curriculum-learning claim, and the main robustness, performance, transferability, and consistency-analysis claims retain their scope.

C2.justification: Sections 3 and 5.4 remove explicit assertions of model-agnostic properties or nature, retaining statements about integration and generalization across different backbones. This modestly softens the applicability characterization. Mechanism explanations and the panorama-training limitation remain unchanged.

D1.justification: The corrected probability endpoints in Section 5.1 improve the accuracy of implementation instructions and agree with Section 3.2's increasing-probability curriculum. Other hyperparameters, code-access information, software versions, and hardware details remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works and substantive research positioning remain unchanged. Section 2 deletes a criticism of distortion in transformation-based pipelines, but the introduction retains that criticism; the abstract also retains the curriculum-learning novelty claim.

P1.justification: Localized edits revise the abstract's consistency wording, rewrite the first contribution bullet, remove a related-work sentence, and replace model-agnostic terminology. The affiliation is expanded and corresponding-author emails are added. Section organization remains unchanged.

P2.justification: Expanded front matter and the added email footnote cause small text and column reflows. Figures, tables, captions, and their placement remain unchanged; all supplementary pages render identically.

improvement.justification: Changing the reported rotation schedule to 0%–75% resolves the contradiction between Section 5.1 and the increasing-probability curriculum in Sections 3.1–3.2, improving reproducibility. The applicability wording is also more restrained. Experimental results and supplementary evidence remain unchanged, so the overall gain is limited.
